title: No Verified Incident Can Support Claims About Vietnam’s Dog Trade
excerpt: Current source material contains no verified incident, official dataset, court record, or health alert. Claims about stolen pets, poison, and disease risk require documented evidence before publication.
body_html:
No court verdict, police seizure, intercepted shipment, or emergency health alert is documented in the available source material. That leaves no verified incident from which to claim cyanide bait, stolen family companions, uninspected meat, or a specific trade-linked disease event. Publishing those claims without records would mislead readers and weaken Vietnamese-led reform.

Evidence must carry the charge

Claims about pet theft require named authorities, dates, locations, case numbers, or credible reporting. Claims about commercial transport require seizure records, inspection findings, quarantine documents, or court evidence. Claims about rabies require clear separation between household exposure and commercial supply chains. Those are parallel biosecurity concerns unless primary evidence proves a direct connection.

Rabies facts remain urgent

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Treatment must begin before symptoms develop; once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance sets out these medical facts.

Demand records. Demand reform.

Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, and local officials need transparent enforcement records, humane animal-control systems, traceable transport, and accountable quarantine. The SDE campaign calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to that public demand while following campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
